messages.content: Explain why the Moon appears to change shape during a month.

response:
The moon appears to change shape because different portions of its sunlit side are facing us as it moves in its orbit. The moon orbits the Earth in about 29.5 days, and because it is tidally locked, the same side always faces the Earth — but the portion facing toward the sun is gradually shifting.

At new moon, the side of the moon facing Earth is in darkness because the facing side is all on the far side of the body from the sun. As the moon orbits, more and more of the sunlit side becomes visible from Earth, forming the phases: crescent, first quarter, gibbous, full, and then waning gibbous, third quarter, and back to new.

Conversely, the dark side is always facing away from the Earth, which is why the hemisphere of the moon facing us never experiences darkness — it is always half lit. The variation in which lit half is facing us gives us the different phase shapes.
